Introduction

What Is a Partnership Firm?

A Partnership Firm is formed when two or more people agree to share the profits of a business run by all or any of them, governed by the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. The relationship is defined by a partnership deed that sets out profit-sharing, roles and responsibilities.

Registration with the Registrar of Firms is optional but strongly recommended — it strengthens the firm's legal standing, particularly if a dispute ever needs to go to court.

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Simple and inexpensive to set up compared to a company
  • Flexible profit-sharing and management terms via the deed
  • Fewer compliance requirements than an LLP or company
  • Registration (if done) strengthens legal standing in disputes

Disadvantages

  • Unlimited liability — partners are personally liable for firm debts
  • No separate legal identity distinct from the partners
  • An unregistered firm cannot sue third parties in certain situations
  • Can be harder to raise external funding than an LLP or company

Eligibility

Who Can Form a Partnership

  • Minimum 2 partners, maximum 50 partners
  • All partners must be of legal age and sound mind
  • A partnership deed setting out terms agreed by all partners
  • A registered business address

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Draft the Partnership Deed

We draft a deed covering profit-sharing, capital contribution, roles, and dispute resolution terms.

2. Execute & Notarise

All partners sign the deed, which is then notarised on stamp paper of the applicable value.

3. Register with the Registrar of Firms

File the application along with the deed and required documents — optional but recommended.

4. PAN, GST & Bank Account

Apply for the firm's PAN, GST registration if applicable, and open a current bank account. Timelines can vary by state and bank.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN and Aadhaar of all partners
  • Passport-size photographs of all partners
  • Proof of business address (utility bill + NOC, if rented)
  • Partnership deed on appropriate stamp paper

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements

  • Income tax return filing for the firm
  • GST return filing, if registered
  • Tax audit, if turnover crosses the applicable threshold
  • Updating the partnership deed when partners or terms change
